LESSON: WRITING 4.3.1 ESSAY WRITING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we describe events, people and things accurately?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the steps involved in writing a descriptive essay for information
2. write a descriptive essay for effective communication
3. recognise the role of writing on various topics for creative expression and enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 4.3.1 ESSAY WRITING
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 4.3.1 ESSAY WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Explain the steps involved in writing a descriptive essay for information

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the steps involved in writing a descriptive essay for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the steps involved in writing a descriptive essay for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the steps involved in writing a descriptive essay for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a descriptive essay for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to write a descriptive essay for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a descriptive essay for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a descriptive essay for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Recognise the role of writing on various topics for creative expression and enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the role of writing on various topics for creative expression and enjoyment. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the role of writing on various topics for creative expression and enjoyment.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the role of writing on various topics for creative expression and enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain the steps involved in writing a descriptive essay for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing to a partner. (skill: write a descriptive essay for effective communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: recognise the role of writing on various topics for creative expression and enjoyment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the steps involved in writing a descriptive essay for information.
3. Practise this skill: write a descriptive essay for effective communication.
4. Practise this skill: recognise the role of writing on various topics for creative expression and enjoyment.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we describe events, people and things accurately?
2. How should one behave in public places to avoid putting others in danger?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the steps involved in writing a descriptive essay for information.
5. Be able to: write a descriptive essay for effective communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
